applicability.note: THE GENERAL SHAPE, AND IT EXPLAINS A WHOLE CLASS OF 'THE PORTAL IGNORED MY QUERY'. On NovusAGENDA's MeetingsResponsive.aspx the visible date inputs txtCalendarFrom and txtCalendarTo carry the DISABLED attribute, and the hidden hfFromDate/hfToDate beside them are written by the ddlDateRange <select> ('Last Month', 'Last Year', 'Custom Date Range', ...). A POST that sets the hidden fields and submits btnSearch therefore sets a value the server recomputes from the dropdown before the search runs, and the response echoes the DEFAULT window rather than the requested one. THE DIAGNOSTIC IS THE ECHO: read back whatever the page reports the applied window to be, and compare it to the window you asked for. Equal means the query ran; different means it did not, and a zero-row result from a query that did not run is a FAILED extraction and never an absence. THE FIX IS TO OPERATE THE CONTROL THAT OWNS THE VALUE: select the named window, or select 'Custom Date Range' — which is what ENABLES the text boxes — and then type into them. A browser at rung 6 finds this in one step because it refuses to click a disabled element and says so; a hand-built POST cannot find it at all, because a disabled input is still serialisable and still ignored.

routes.title: the instrument check that has to happen before a zero-row result is written down as anything at all

applicability.note: A ZERO IS A CLAIM ABOUT A GOVERNMENT AND AN INSTRUMENT AT THE SAME TIME, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS USUALLY CHECKED. A selector that matches nothing, a table id that changed, a grid that renders after the read — each returns zero, and each reads identically to a body that publishes nothing. THE CHECK IS TO MAKE THE SAME READER RETURN NON-ZERO, in the same session, against something it should find: a wider window, an older year, a sibling tenant, a different body on the same platform. Rosters answer who someone IS; almost nothing answers what they have DONE, and a question about an official's year is unanswerable without it. routes.title: the denominator read that decides whether a 'missing rows' report is about the pipeline or about the publisher

applicability.note: A READER SAYING 'THE MEETINGS ARE MISSING' IS A CLAIM ABOUT A SURFACE, AND IT HAS TWO COMPLETELY DIFFERENT CAUSES THAT LOOK IDENTICAL. Either rows are being lost between the source and the screen, or the source never had them. THE CHEAP DISCRIMINATOR RUNS FIRST AND IS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN: the snapshot records fetched, normalized and drops-by-reason per source. If fetched equals normalized and the drops are accounted, no row was lost and the pipeline is not the suspect — which is a strictly stronger statement than 'the code looks right'. THEN ASK THE PRIMARY SOURCE THE SAME QUESTION THE ADAPTER ASKED, by hand, over the same window: if the API returns what the snapshot holds, the adapter is exonerated by observation rather than by inspection. Only then is the question about the publisher, and only then is it worth hunting other routes. routes.title: a byte grep over a born-digital PDF finds nothing on a document that says it plainly, and the nothing becomes a false absence

A prior walk recorded that an enacted Arizona bill has NO PUBLISHED SIGNING DATE, on the evidence that grepping a chaptered version for approved|governor|filed returned nothing. The grep was run over the PDF's BYTES. A born-digital PDF stores its text inside FlateDecode content streams, so a byte grep cannot match ordinary words in it and returns nothing regardless of what the document says — the measurement was guaranteed to produce that answer before it was run. MEASURED CORRECTLY 2026-08-28: extract the text layer first, and every chaptered version at https://www.azleg.gov/legtext/57Leg/2R/laws/<NNNN>.pdf ends with its own enactment stamp — 'APPROVED BY THE GOVERNOR FEBRUARY 6, 2026. FILED IN THE OFFICE OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE FEBRUARY 6, 2026.' That is a signing date, published by the state, in the primary document, for every enacted bill. THE GENERAL RULE: NEVER grep, regex or string-search a PDF, a DOCX or any compressed container directly. Run the extraction layer and search ITS OUTPUT, and if the extraction returns nothing, that is a finding about the extraction. It produces a confident, specific, plausible-sounding absence — 'the state does not publish signing dates' — which is a false claim about a government, and it then hardens into a NAMED GAP that later sessions inherit and cite. A SECOND LESSON FROM THE SAME DOCUMENT: read the stamp's WORDING, not just its date. A bill reaches a chapter three ways — approved by the governor, becoming law without signature, or passage over a veto — so 'chaptered' proves ENACTMENT and never proves a SIGNATURE, and filing every chapter as 'signed' is its own false claim about a governmental act.

routes.title: a body's own official web page, not its vendor portal, publishes the dated public events of an effort it runs; read them in a fixed structural order and HOLD every event that cannot be verified

applicability.note: THE MISS THIS PREVENTS: a body's committee meetings and community engagement sessions for a named effort (a school reconfiguration, a bond, a facilities plan) are published on the body's own CMS page for that effort and nowhere on the meeting portal a meetings adapter reads, so a portal-only walk never sees them. WHAT THE PAGE LOOKS LIKE: a district or city CMS page carrying (1) prose statements such as 'Joint Committee Meeting Sept. 11, 2026', 'Next Meeting October 1, 2026' and 'Joint Committee Meeting Aug 29, 2026 ... 9AM to 4PM'; (2) structured event cards with a title, a date such as '9/23/2026', a time range such as '4:00pm - 6:30pm', an event name, and venue lines such as 'Cholla High School' / 'South Gym'; (3) RSVP and livestream links. THE EXTRACTION ORDER (lib/sources/official-page-events/): schema.org Event JSON-LD; then embedded event state (a CMS that renders its event list client-side from an inline JSON.parse("...") literal or an application/json script, each record carrying a title and an offset-bearing start_at, as Apptegy/Thrillshare district sites do); then microdata Event; then linked .ics files (retrieved only on an authorized host); then structured event cards (an element whose class or id names an event, grown to the smallest wrapper that still holds exactly one date: date + time range + venue line, the most specific venue line winning); then dated headings ('Joint Committee Meeting Sept. 11, 2026', whose own block may state the time 'from 9AM to 4PM' when it names no other date); then 'Next meeting <Month D, YYYY>' statements, titled from the heading of the block that carries them. A PURE route check for discovery shares the same rules: verifyOfficialPageEvents({ body, url, html, now }) returns YIELDED, EMPTY or NOT_CONFIRMED with the verified sample events and every held event's reasons. VERIFICATION, every rule of which HOLDS the event with a named reason instead of guessing: the page host must equal the body's registered official domain or be explicitly authorized in the wiring; each date must parse unambiguously and fall inside the serving window (a day named without a year, such as 'September 21st', is ambiguous); the event title must name the body or its committee. RENDERING RULES the extractor keeps: a date with no time is date-only (startPrecision DAY), never a guessed time, and a range whose start has no am/pm is not read; a venue the page does not state is the publisher's named gap (venueGap NOT_STATED_BY_PUBLISHER) and a stated venue with no reviewed coordinates is carried verbatim as our gap (STATED_NOT_PLACED), never pinned; an end equal to the start is no end; the event type is preserved as published (a Joint Committee meeting or a community engagement session) and never inflated into a Governing Board meeting; an event is cancelled only when the page says so; provenance is the page URL plus the evidence excerpt the event was read from. TRANSPORT: the recording session observed curl receive a Cloudflare 520 from www.tusd1.org while a Node fetch with the project user agent (politeGetText, lib/sources/http.ts) received HTTP 200 for the same page, so a refused curl is not a wall here. robots.txt was read first and allowed the page (it disallows only /TUSD-school-exit-survey and /PLC-Roskruge).
